test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the name of the ship on which two female officers of the Indian Navy completed a historic circumnavigation in May 2025, as part of the Navika Sagar Parikrama II mission?
solution:
The correct answer is __**INS Tarini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Navika Sagar Parikrama II** is the **second edition** of the **Indian Navy's** ambitious global circumnavigation expedition, featuring two courageous female officers, **Lieutenant Commander Roopa A** and **Lieutenant Commander Dilna K**.
 
• The mission was conducted aboard the **Indian Naval Sailing Vessel (INSV) Tarini**, which is a **56-foot** sailing yacht built indigenously in **India** by **M/s Aquarius Shipyard Pvt Ltd** located in **Goa**. ***Hence, the correct answer is INS Tarini.***
 
• The expedition is a historic **double-handed circumnavigation**, meaning it was completed by only two crew members without any external assistance or use of fossil fuels for propulsion, relying entirely on **wind power**.
 
• The voyage was flagged off from **Ocean Sailing Node** at **INS Mandovi**, **Goa**, in **October 2024** and successfully concluded in **May 2025**, covering a distance of approximately **21,600 nautical miles**.
 
• This mission follows the legacy of **Navika Sagar Parikrama I**, which took place in **2017-2018**, but sets a new record as the first **double-handed** global voyage by **Indian women**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vessel Characteristics:** **INSV Tarini** was inducted into the **Indian Navy** in **February 2017**. It is designed for extreme ocean conditions and is equipped with advanced **satellite navigation** and communication systems. The boat is named after the **Tara Tarini** temple in **Odisha**, which is dedicated to the patron deity of sailors.
 
• **Training and Mentorship:** The two officers, **Lt Cdr Dilna K** and **Lt Cdr Roopa A**, underwent rigorous training for over **three years**. They were mentored by **Commander Abhilash Tomy (Retd)**, a **Kirti Chakra** recipient and the first Indian to complete a solo, non-stop circumnavigation under sail.
 
• **Mission Route:** The route taken by **INSV Tarini** during this mission involved crossing the **equator** twice and rounding the three great Capes: **Cape Leeuwin**, **Cape Horn**, and the **Cape of Good Hope**, traversing the **Indian**, **Pacific**, and **Atlantic Oceans**.
 
• **Objectives:** The primary objective of **Navika Sagar Parikrama II** is to promote **Nari Shakti** (women empowerment) and showcase **India’s** indigenous shipbuilding capabilities under the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative. It also aims to encourage **maritime adventure** and enhance the **Indian Navy's** global footprint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Previous Missions:** While **Navika Sagar Parikrama I** featured a **six-member** all-woman crew led by **Lieutenant Commander Vartika Joshi**, the **2024-25 mission** was significantly more challenging due to the **reduced crew size** (only two officers), requiring them to manage all navigation, maintenance, and weather routing duties in shifts.
 
• **Environmental and Scientific Impact:** Throughout the journey, the crew collected **meteorological and oceanographic data**, which is vital for **climate change** research and improving weather forecasting models for the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• **National Significance:** The successful completion of the mission in **May 2025** was celebrated as a major milestone in **Indian maritime history**, further solidifying **India's** status as a leading maritime nation with highly skilled naval personnel.
